recommendation_summary: Act now: put the lead and both qualified engineers on every change as reviewers, and let any one of the three approve. Then track the time from 'ready for review' to 'approved' in the existing tracker. Optional additions: none. Conditional later step: if waits still go past a day, agree who reviews on which day. Unmet needs: none; this fixes the absent-lead approval wait at no cost.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You asked that changes stop waiting for approval when the lead is absent, so the team ships faster.
labels.Deleted: Spotify squads and chapters, Jira Align, quarterly planning workshops, and new tooling spend. None of them addresses approval waits; four engineers in one time zone already have a working tracker.
labels.Bottleneck: Approval. In each of the last six changes, coding took under a day, then the change waited three days because the lead, the only assigned reviewer, was away.
labels.Checked myself: Only what you told me: the six changes, the sole-reviewer assignment, the lead's absence, and that two other engineers are qualified and authorized to approve.

note: The reply bounds the fix to reviewer coverage, explicitly drops squads/chapters, Jira Align and the workshops, and grounds its check only in the facts the user supplied.
